accuracy.evidence: Sub-shell capacities (s 2, p 6, d 10), one orbital holding two electrons of opposite spin (Pauli), the 1s 2s 2p 3s 3p 4s 3d filling order for Z = 1 to 20, Hund's rule, s spherical and p dumbbell orbitals along x, y and z all match the OCR/AQA A-level specifications and the LibreTexts and RSC notes. Every configuration the lab writes is generated from the same fill function and spot-checked: C 1s² 2s² 2p², N 2p³ (3 unpaired), O 2p⁴ (2 unpaired), Cl 3s² 3p⁵, K 4s¹, Ca 4s².

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented A-level slips: a p sub-shell holding only 2 (challenge distractor built by capping p at 2), pairing in one p orbital before the others are singly filled (live Hund-slip flag and pair-first distractor), placing potassium's 19th electron in 3d (prediction, task and 3d-first distractor), superscripts not summing to Z, an orbital as a fixed planetary path (mastery m7), and confusing one orbital's 2 with a shell's 8 (opening prediction).

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab is an energy-ordered orbital box diagram with tap-to-spin electrons, live Aufbau and Hund violation detection, an orbital-shape inset that draws the selected s sphere or p dumbbell on axes, and a configuration string written from the boxes. The existing shells lab (flagshell) drops electrons onto rings around a nucleus with no sub-shells, spins or shapes; nothing here could be relabelled for another topic.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners discover rules by doing: building carbon by hand and seeing the Hund flag if they pair in 2p, watching the unpaired count go 3 then 2 from nitrogen to oxygen, choosing a box for potassium's 19th electron and seeing the Aufbau flag if they use 3d, and splitting chlorine's 2, 8, 7 into 1s² / 2s² 2p⁶ / 3s² 3p⁵. The step text only confirms afterwards.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions precede the actions, each with a tempting wrong option: an orbital holds 8 like a shell, carbon's 2p electrons pair in one box, nitrogen has 1 or 5 unpaired, potassium's electron goes to 3d because shell 3 has room, and shell 2 is 2s⁸ or 2p⁸. The next task shows the answer on the diagram.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Twelve rotating questions alternate between picking a ground-state configuration and counting unpaired electrons. Each wrong option carries its own message naming the slip: 3d before 4s, p holding only 2, superscripts not adding to the atomic number, pairing before Hund's rule allows, or treating every p electron as unpaired. The diagram then fills to show the right answer.

readability.evidence: Learner paragraphs use short sentences and define orbital, sub-shell and Hund's rule once each in plain words. Canvas text is one heading line (the configuration) and one status line, and challenge feedback is one sentence plus the answer. Within the validator's readability limits.

no_filler.evidence: Each paragraph carries a fact or rule: capacities, orbital shapes, filling order with the 4s/3d reason, Hund's rule and how to write a configuration. The adult text names the specific mistakes and two check questions; there is no scene-setting or praise padding.

mobile.evidence: At 390 px the seven sub-shell rows stack by energy with boxes up to 30 px plus a 3 px hit margin, the shape inset sits in the free right-hand space, the status text wraps inside the canvas, and the box selector and step buttons wrap below. Checked in the iPhone 13 walkthrough in both themes.

accessibility.evidence: Every tap has a button twin: a previous/next box selector with an add-electron button (third press empties), Empty all, plus one-electron-by-the-rules and remove buttons from step 4. Shape buttons cover step 1. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every change with the configuration, element, unpaired count and any rule slip; axe is clean in both themes.
